title: How to Dress for Your Body Type: A Guide to Every Shape
summary: Measure yourself, find your body shape with our calculator and discover how to dress it in clothes that fit, feel and look great, courtesy of Stitch Fix.
body_markdown:
Your body shape is all about the natural proportions between your shoulders, bust, waist and hips—it’s about structure, not your size or weight. Understanding those proportions makes picking silhouettes, fits and styling details effortless, giving you total freedom to highlight what you love to show off.


At Stitch Fix, we believe every body should be celebrated—not restricted by old “do’s and don’ts” or told to hide “problem areas.” You get to decide what looks and feels good on you, and if you love something, you should wear it. That said, learning how to identify and dress for your body shape can simplify daily closet decisions and[build your style confidence](https://www.stitchfix.com/women/blog/style-guide/how-to-find-your-personal-style/) . Let’s dive in!


## **How to Identify Your Body Shape**


Your body shape is simply the natural relationship between four key points: your shoulders, bust, waist and hips—and it’s entirely separate from your size or weight. To make daily dressing even easier, our Stylists will walk you through taking quick measurements, using our interactive shape calculator and exploring the five common body shapes you might resonate with most.


### **How to Measure Your Shoulders, Bust, Waist and Hips**


Grab a flexible tape measure and stand in front of a mirror for your most accurate numbers. For best results, measure over form-fitting clothing or undergarments rather than bulky layers to capture your true fit.


- **Shoulders:** Measure straight across your back from the outer edge of one shoulder bone to the other to establish your upper-body frame
- **Bust:** Wrap the tape around the fullest part of your bust, keeping it level across your back to capture your top-half proportion
- **Waist:** Measure around the narrowest part of your natural waistline (usually just above your belly button) to gauge your midsection definition
- **Hips:** Stand with your feet together and measure around the fullest part of your hips and rear to complete your silhouette baseline.


### **Use the Body Shape Calculator**


Plug your measurements into our body shape calculator to see which silhouette naturally aligns with your proportions.

### **The 5 Common Body Shapes**


Body shape is purely about your structural balance—never your size or weight. While every body is wonderfully unique, most fall closest to one of these five common shapes:


- **Triangle Shape (also called Pear)**
- **Hourglass Shape (often described as Curvy)**
- **Heart Shape (also known as Inverted Triangle)**
- **Rectangle Shape (Hips and shoulders are in proportional alignment)**
- **Oval Shape (also known as round)**


## **Styling Goals by Body Shape**


**Body Shape** **Main Styling Goal**


**Triangle (Pear)** **Draw focus upward with statement necklines while accentuating your lower half**


**Hourglass (Curvy)** **Celebrate your naturally defined waistline and balanced silhouette**


**Heart (Inverted Triangle)** **Showcase your strong shoulder frame and play with breezy volume through your hips**


**Rectangle (Athletic)** **Experiment with effortless waist definition, layering and playful proportions**


**Oval (Round)** **Show off your arms and legs while enjoying comfortable, fluid silhouettes**


## **How to Dress for Each Body Type**


### **Triangle Body Type (Pear)**


You identify with this shape if…


- Your hips and rear are fuller than your bust line
- Your waist is narrower than your hips
- Your shoulders are narrower in comparison


**Styling goal:** Draw focus upward with statement necklines while accentuating your lower half.


**What to wear:** Structured jackets, statement sleeves and boat necklines that bring structure to your shoulders; breezy A-line skirts and straight-leg denim that drape over your hips; vibrant colors or bold patterns up top to pull the eye upward. Look for fluid, unlined fabrics or wide-leg silhouettes that move with you all day long.


See the full[triangle styling guide](https://www.stitchfix.com/women/blog/style-guide/how-to-dress-a-triangle-body-shape/) for more ideas.


### **Hourglass Body Type (Curvy)**


You may be this body type if…


- Your bust and hip measurements are balanced
- You have a naturally defined waistline
- You describe your frame as curvy through your bust, hips and thighs


**Styling goal:** Celebrate your naturally defined waistline while keeping your silhouette balanced.


**What to wear:** Wrap dresses and belted silhouettes that highlight your waist; fitted tops paired with pencil or full skirts; open V-necks that follow your natural lines. Bring instant waist definition with a gentle front-tuck or a slender belt.


See the full[hourglass styling guide](https://www.stitchfix.com/women/blog/styling-hourglass-figure/) for more inspiration.


### **Heart Body Type (Inverted Triangle)**


You might identify with this shape if…


- Your shoulders are broader than your hips
- Your frame is straighter through your hips and lower body
- Your upper body establishes your main silhouette line


**Styling goal:** Showcase your strong shoulder frame while adding breezy volume and movement to your lower half.


**What to wear:** V-necks and scoop necklines that elongate the look of your torso; A-line skirts, wide-leg trousers and flared denim that add volume below; patch pockets or pleating on your bottom half. Also try raglan sleeves, soft knits or unconstructed jackets.


See the full[heart body shape styling guide](https://www.stitchfix.com/women/blog/style-guide/how-to-dress-for-a-heart-body-shape/) for more ideas.


### **Rectangle Body Type (Athletic)**


You may be this body type if…


- Your shoulder, bust and hip measurements align evenly
- Your waist is straight rather than deeply defined
- Your weight is distributed evenly across your frame


**Styling goal:** Experiment with dynamic layers, fun proportions and effortless waist definition.


**What to wear:** Belted dresses and cinch-waist tops; peplum styles, ruffles and textured fabrics that add dimension; high-waisted bottoms that highlight your midsection. Try playing with cropped jackets or bold prints to build instant visual texture.


See the full[rectangle styling guide](https://www.stitchfix.com/women/blog/how-to-dress-a-rectangle-body-shape/) for more ideas.


### **Oval Body Type (Apple)**


You might identify with this shape if…


- Your waist measurement is fuller than your shoulders and hips
- Your shoulders and hips are proportional in width
- You have shapely arms, shoulders and legs


**Styling goal:** Show off your arms and legs while enjoying comfortable, fluid silhouettes.


**What to wear:** Empire-waist tops and A-line dresses that skim gracefully; elongating V-necks; tailored pants and fitted sleeves that highlight your legs and arms. Choose soft knits and woven fabrics with subtle stretch for a feel-good fit that offers movement without clinging.


See the full[oval styling guide](https://www.stitchfix.com/women/blog/style-guide/styling-oval-figure/) for more ideas.


## **Dress for Your Body Shape with Stitch Fix**


Every body and every silhouette is unique. If you don’t fit neatly into a single category, that’s completely normal! Many women are a natural mix of different shapes. These suggestions are simply a starting point to help you[find what works for your body](https://www.stitchfix.com/find-your-perfect-fit) . It’s all about mixing, matching and discovering what’s best for you.


Ready to flaunt your favorite features with new silhouettes? Finding the perfect fit is kind of our thing.
